content.title: About
content.content: An egg omelet with fresh vegetables (excluding dark‑green leafy vegetables and tomatoes) is cooked in a pan with a small amount of added fat. Eggs provide a complete set of proteins, while the vegetables add vitamins and fiber. The dish is suitable for breakfast or a light lunch.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The omelet can be prepared in 5–7 minutes, making it a quick meal option.
Adding a modest amount of butter or oil enhances flavor and helps absorb fat‑soluble vitamins from the vegetables.
Eggs are one of the most affordable sources of vitamin D.
The recipe is highly adaptable; you can change the vegetable mix to suit your taste.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs contain all essential amino acids, making them an excellent source of complete protein.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Both eggs and vegetables provide B12, riboflavin, and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and carotenoids
items.content: Vegetables such as carrots or bell peppers add beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Monounsaturated fats from the added oil can help lower LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: Fiber and minerals
items.content: Vegetables contribute dietary fiber, potassium, and magnesium, supporting normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg proteins.

items.title: Excess fat intake
items.content: Using too much oil or butter increases the calorie density of the dish.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Eggs should be fully cooked to reduce the risk of salmonella infection.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the omelet hot, optionally topped with fresh herbs (parsley, dill) and a modest amount of low‑fat cheese. It can be cut into wedges and eaten with a fork, or paired with whole‑grain toast.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The omelet is best enjoyed immediately. If needed, store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours and reheat before serving.
